key_insight: Capping planar hot-pressed CsPbBr3 thin films with few-layer hBN greatly improves heat dissipation without changing the perovskite’s morphology or optical behavior.
engineering_relevance: This provides a practical thermal-management strategy for perovskite optoelectronic devices operating under high excitation or high-power conditions.
method: Large-scale semidry transfer of 2D hBN onto planar hot-pressed CsPbBr3 thin films
Microscopic and spectroscopic characterization to verify film integrity and optical preservation
Heat-diffusion simulation to compare capping-layer thermal performance
evidence_signal: The heterostructure reached an estimated thermal conductivity of 3 W/(m·K), about 7× higher than bare CsPbBr3 films (0.45 W/(m·K)), and showed reduced laser-induced heating under continuous-wave excitation.
watch_item: Device integration must preserve the perovskite interface and uniform hBN coverage; transfer quality and scalability may affect reproducibility.
paper_title: Improved Heat Dissipation in CsPbBr${_3}$-hBN Heterostructures
